decompile: 2026-09-24 third pass (REPORT §10): on HTTP 401, or the 4-Series client's synthetic 666, the library logs out. A 401's 'Unauthorized' is mapped to 'Incorrect Username or Password...', which deletes the cached token, so re-login fetches a fresh one. PersistentLogin: up to 5 immediate re-logins, then a 5-minute wait. At most two such waits happen, and each resets the counter, so each can be followed by another burst of up to 5. A 60 s CameraStatus keep-alive runs only after a freshly issued token, not after a cached one is reused.
summary: Session recovery differs. The Crestron PersistentLogin retries 5 times, waits 5 minutes, then stops until a program restart; per [AVX-3179] the module logs the user out on a permission error. Both Extron drivers re-request a token on every (re)connect and retry immediately and without limit when a reply lacks `token`. In CS that retry is direct recursion (TokenRequestHandler → TokenRequest), so a device answering 200 without a token and without status 'Error' would end in RecursionError. GC re-queues through DriverCmd, which is opaque.

update: 2026-09-24 second pass: the library caches a token per device IP on the processor's disk, checks 1.5 s after an IP arrives, logs in only if none is stored; PersistentLogin is new in v1.2 (§8).
